key_insight: A coherent Hue–Saturation–Lightness structure emerges in the VAE latent space of the FLUX text-to-image model: a low-dimensional Latent Color Subspace (LCS) that encodes color semantics and enables predictable color manipulation.
problem_solved: Lack of fine-grained, interpretable control over color in text-to-image generation due to poor understanding of how color is encoded in high-dimensional latent spaces.
method: Analyze FLUX VAE latent vectors to identify directions and subspaces that correlate with perceptual color attributes (Hue, Saturation, Lightness).
Quantify correlations and build linear predictors to map latent coordinates to H/S/L values; validate by predicting color attributes of generated images.
Manipulate latent codes along the discovered subspace to perform controlled color edits and evaluate visual consistency and semantic preservation.
impact: Provides a simple, interpretable mechanism for color control and editing in generative models, improving usability for artists and researchers and advancing latent-space interpretability for downstream tasks.

paper_title: The Latent Color Subspace: Emergent Order in High-Dimensional Chaos
paper_authors: Mateusz Pach, Jessica Bader, Quentin Bouniot, Serge Belongie, Zeynep Akata
